Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed collision in a parking lot with a complaint of right knee pain and reduced range of
motion. The reported mechanism of injury is consistent with the force of the impact and the pattern of symptoms described. Over
the course of 22 visits, care progressed along a typical rehabilitation pathway, including physical therapy, activity modification,
and anti-inflammatory management. Visit frequency decreased steadily as symptoms improved and functional goals were met.
Examination revealed localized tenderness and mild effusion along the medial joint line, findings that support the reported injury.
Other orthopedic tests, including ligament stability assessment and neurovascular checks, were within normal limits. No prior
injury or treatment involving the same body region is documented in the patient's history. Billing records reflect single,
appropriate charges for each service rendered, with no duplicated entries. At discharge, the pateint was ambulating without
assistance and reported minimal residual discomfort with prolonged standing.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
